topic: Mastering the Product and Chain Rules in Calculus

sections.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: The Concept of Change
sections.content: Briefly revisit the derivative as the rate of change (slope of the tangent line). Visualize a 'Robot Runner' whose velocity is defined by the product or composition of two simpler functions.
sections.example: Visualizing f(x) = x^2 and g(x) = sin(x) as two independent 'gears' moving at different rates.

sections.title: The Product Rule: The Collaborative Effort
sections.content: Introduce the Product Rule for differentiating the product of two functions. Use an animation of a rectangle expanding: when width and height both change, the change in area is the sum of two rectangular strips.
sections.example: Differentiating f(x) = x^2 * sin(x). Formula: f'g + fg'. Imagine an animal growing in both length and height simultaneously; the total size increase is the sum of these two growth dimensions.

sections.title: The Chain Rule: The Nested Function
sections.content: Explain the Chain Rule for composite functions: f(g(x)). Use the 'Matryoshka Doll' analogy—to get to the center, you must account for the rate of change of the outer shell multiplied by the rate of change of the inner doll.
sections.example: Differentiating y = sin(x^2). The outer function is sin(u) and inner is u = x^2. Chain: d/dx = cos(x^2) * 2x.

sections.title: Synthesis & Complex Application
sections.content: Combine both rules in a single challenging problem. Show the logical step-by-step breakdown of how to identify which rule to apply first.
sections.example: Differentiating h(x) = (x^2 + 1)^3 * cos(x). Step 1: Identify as Product Rule (u*v). Step 2: Use Chain Rule to find the derivative of (x^2+1)^3.

sections.title: Quick Review & Visual Summary
sections.content: A high-speed recap using a flowchart graphic. Product Rule (Addition of two terms) vs. Chain Rule (Multiplication of two derivatives).
sections.example: A 'Cheat Sheet' slide showing: [u*v]' = u'v + uv' vs [f(g(x))]' = f'(g(x)) * g'(x).
